nodes.label: UZCASTING Platform
nodes.rationale: Single monorepo holding three products (Spring Boot backend, React admin panel, Expo mobile app). Scope is a video streaming + casting platform; the older 'social network / messenger' concept was explicitly dropped.

nodes.label: Frozen Legacy Casting Module
nodes.rationale: Legacy Controller/Entity/Repository/Services packages and their paths are frozen because live clients (Telegram bot, old admin site /aadmin/*, mobile app) are deployed separately and are never updated in lockstep; changing a path breaks all of them at once.

nodes.label: /app Namespace Separation
nodes.rationale: All new routes live under backend /api/v1/app/** and frontend /app/** so the two spaces can never collide; adding a new endpoint requires neither reading nor touching legacy code, removing the possibility of accidentally breaking old clients. One exception: app users still authenticate through the legacy POST /api/v1/auth/login.

nodes.label: OldCastingFrozenTest
nodes.rationale: Encodes the freeze in code rather than prose: build fails if a legacy controller is moved, renamed, has an endpoint path changed, or if a new controller is added to the legacy package.

nodes.label: ExistingCastingRegressionTest
nodes.rationale: Guards the end-to-end casting flow (application form, accept/reject, bot message) against regression.

nodes.label: AdminEndpointGuardTest
nodes.rationale: Architecture test that forbids adding an unguarded admin endpoint — hiding a menu item is not security, every endpoint is re-checked on the backend.

nodes.label: Five-Role Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: HYPER_ADMIN(100) > SUPER_ADMIN(80) > ADMIN(60) > WORKER(40) > USER(10). Nobody can grant a permission they lack, nobody can manage an equal or higher role, and nobody can edit their own account. Viewing and managing are deliberately separated so HYPER_ADMIN can audit all staff accounts.

nodes.label: Single HYPER_ADMIN Rule
nodes.rationale: HYPER_ADMIN cannot create an equal role: two HYPER_ADMINs could not delete each other, so one stolen account could spawn accounts nobody could remove. Recovery of a lost HYPER_ADMIN happens server-side via environment.

nodes.label: 43-Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Permissions are meaningful only for WORKER; ADMIN and above bypass the table entirely and are limited only by role hierarchy.

nodes.label: Permissions Read Per Request
nodes.rationale: Permissions are not embedded in the JWT but read from the database on every request, so revoking a permission invalidates an already-issued token immediately.

nodes.label: Content Structure Types
nodes.rationale: SINGLE (film, video on the content), EPISODIC (content -> episode, no seasons), SEASONAL (content -> season -> episode). Each episode may consist of several ordered video segments for Reels-style content.

nodes.label: Type vs Category vs Genre
nodes.rationale: Three independent axes most often confused: content type is the shape (one value), category is a catalog section (one, optional), genre is style (many). A category list must therefore never contain names like 'Podcast' or 'Mini series' — those are types, not sections. Guarded by ContentClassificationTest.

nodes.label: Three-Language Publish Rule
nodes.rationale: Translations live in separate tables with UNIQUE(parent_id, locale) rather than a JSON column, so per-language search and indexing work. UZ is mandatory in draft; UZ+RU+EN are all mandatory at publish time — checked at publish, not at save, because content is normally written in one language and translated afterwards.

nodes.label: Chunked Upload Flow
nodes.rationale: Files over 8 MB are uploaded in 5 MB chunks because the production multipart limit is 50 MB and one huge request restarts from zero when it drops. Session is owner-only (others get 404), extension is validated up front, MediaAsset is created only after assembly, abandoned sessions are cleaned after a day, hard cap 5 GB.

nodes.label: Media Raw Delivery
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/app/media/{id}/raw: images public and cached 30 days, videos entitlement-checked. Denial returns 404 not 403 so file existence is not disclosed; paid video gets Cache-Control: no-store; Range/206 supported for seeking; strict CSP on all responses so scripts inside SVG cannot run on the site domain.

nodes.label: Archive Over Delete
nodes.rationale: Media is referenced from 12 places; archiving hides a file from the library while existing references keep working. Deleting an in-use file returns 409 with the exact usage list, because blind deletion means broken images and unplayable video on live pages.

nodes.label: AccessService Entitlement Check
nodes.rationale: Entitlement can come from four sources and is evaluated in exactly one place, not scattered to clients — otherwise the mobile app, the site and the backend would each answer differently. A one-off purchase never grants casting-project access; only active Premium does.

nodes.label: Server-Built Homepage Feed
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/app/home builds the mobile home screen server-side (TZ §31) so adding or reordering a row does not require a new store release. Row order is two-stage (explicit item list wins, otherwise automatic newest-first), section order is changed in one request to avoid an intermediate mixed state, and empty sections are omitted rather than rendered as headerless rows.

nodes.label: Watch Entitlement Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Returns whether playback is allowed, a reason, a requiredAction and prices. When denied, `sources` is empty — a video link is never shipped alongside a refusal — and the file endpoint checks independently, making protection two-layered.

nodes.label: In-Memory Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Token bucket per IP running before the Spring Security chain; exceeding returns 429 with Retry-After. In-memory, so it only covers a single instance — multiple instances would need Redis.

nodes.label: Public Endpoint Allowlist
nodes.rationale: All /api/** is closed except an explicitly enumerated list. casting-user/my/** and /appeal/** remain open only because the Telegram bot flow has no authentication; closing them requires agreement with the bot team.

nodes.label: Telegram Bot Integration
nodes.rationale: The bot posts casting applications (POST /api/v1/casting-user) and uploads photos (POST /api/v1/file/upload) without authentication, which is why those endpoints stay public.

nodes.label: Message Entity Is Not A Messenger
nodes.rationale: The legacy `Message` entity is the accepted/rejected reply sent to the Telegram bot, not chat. Deleting it would mean candidates never receive an answer.
nodes.norm_label: message entity is not a messenger

nodes.label: Deliberate Known Limitations
nodes.rationale: FCM has no key (503 and a FAILED record rather than a fake 'sent'), payment providers are unconnected and the store-billing risk is unresolved, Stars/Coin rate is unset so donation revenue reports null rather than a guess, dev videos are 256 KB of random bytes, search is LIKE '%text%', and the rate limiter is in-memory. Nothing is faked as working.

nodes.label: Future Mobile API Contract
nodes.rationale: TZ §76/§77. Records backend readiness only — no mobile code is written here — so the mobile team does not have to re-derive the backend shape when it starts.

nodes.label: TranslationRules Locale Model
nodes.rationale: No single-field `title` exists; every translation is a separate row with UNIQUE(parent_id, locale), so adding a language needs only a new Locale enum value, not a migration.

nodes.label: Locale Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Request ?lang= wins, then cms_user_account.language, then UZ. Push notifications use only the profile language because there is no request to read.

nodes.label: Modelled But Unopened Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Catalog, content page, search (indexes V21/V23 ready), profile, purchases, comments, ads and /app/auth/** OTP login are modelled in the schema but not exposed yet.

nodes.label: Content ID Stability Guarantee
nodes.rationale: Verified, not assumed: IDs stay Long/IDENTITY (IdStrategyTest §57), are never reused, and content is archived rather than removed (SoftDeleteTest §58).

nodes.label: Slug Is Not Stable
nodes.rationale: Admins can edit the slug, so it is a human-readable address only. Any saved list must key on content_id; keying on slug would break a user's saved items whenever an admin renames content. HomeFeedDto.ContentCard already returns both id and slug.

nodes.label: user_watchlist Future Table
nodes.rationale: 'Watch later' (TZ §77) needs no admin page and no table yet — an empty table would be needless. When added it is just (user_id, content_id) with a unique pair, and the listing must filter archived content so a saved film does not become an unopenable row.

nodes.label: Bunny Stream Video Decision Pending
nodes.rationale: The client proposed delivering video through Bunny Stream ('the server is a turnstile, not a pipe' — no byte passes through the VPS), which contradicts the current local storage + chunked upload + Range design. Video code was deliberately left unchanged until the answer arrives; if accepted, /api/v1/app/watch/* gains a signed HLS link and the app pulls straight from the CDN.

nodes.label: Mobile-Facing Backend Decisions
nodes.rationale: Money is BigDecimal/tiyin because floating point is never used for money (§36); time is Asia/Tashkent (§68); device-limit entity exists but is not enforced until the app connects; unconnected payment providers never return a fake success (§44); FCM writes notifications but does not send, reporting null rather than 0.

nodes.label: Two Backends In One App
nodes.rationale: /api/v1/** (legacy casting: applications, files, news, login) runs on production uzcasting.site; /api/v1/app/** (new platform: home, content, entitlement, media) exists only locally because production still runs the old build.

nodes.label: HomeFeedUnavailableError
nodes.rationale: Production answers GET /api/v1/app/home with 200 but returns the site's index.html because the SPA intercepts unknown paths. Axios does not treat that as an error, so the client must validate the response shape itself.

nodes.label: Phone OTP Login Flow
nodes.rationale: Login and registration are one flow: otp/verify finds the phone's owner or creates a ROLE_USER, exactly as auth/google does. 4-digit code, 3-minute lifetime, BCrypt-hashed in server memory, 2-minute resend cooldown (429 OTP_COOLDOWN), 5 wrong attempts lock the code (429 OTP_LOCKED). Phone is normalised to 998XXXXXXXXX so input format does not matter.

nodes.label: OTP Error Code Translation
nodes.rationale: Backend ApiError{code,message} text is Uzbek-only (TZ §94), so the app translates by code in src/features/auth/otpErrors.ts: OTP_COOLDOWN, OTP_INVALID, OTP_EXPIRED, OTP_LOCKED, SMS_NOT_CONFIGURED, SMS_SEND_FAILED.

nodes.label: Eskiz SMS Gateway
nodes.rationale: Without ESKIZ_EMAIL/ESKIZ_PASSWORD sending fails with 503 SMS_NOT_CONFIGURED on purpose — a silent 'success' with no SMS would be worse, mirroring the Google-without-keys behaviour. The app.otp.message-template text must match the template approved in the Eskiz cabinet or the gateway rejects the send.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/casting-user/web Catalog
nodes.rationale: Live endpoint returning real casting profiles (~68 KB). Client rules mirrored from the site: show only photos with isWebShow true and drop profiles with none, compute age from birthday when absent, lowercase castingType.

nodes.label: Public PII Exposure Finding
nodes.rationale: The unauthenticated catalog returns phone, email, telegram, instagram, exact birthdate and body measurements including for minors (an age:17 record). The mobile Creator type deliberately omits them, but the fix belongs on the backend: serve only showcase fields publicly and move contacts behind an authenticated request, which also cuts the 68 KB payload.

nodes.label: SecurityConfig permitAll On Everything
nodes.rationale: Root cause of the PII leak: SecurityConfig permits GET/POST/PUT/DELETE on /** without a token, so the JWT filter — written and working — has nothing left to enforce, including on admin and write endpoints. Fix is to narrow permitAll to genuinely public routes and mark the rest .authenticated() with role checks.

nodes.label: castingType vs TZ Categories Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Only 4 of the 10 TZ directions exist in the database (actor, model, bloger, influencer); six are missing and two DB types (euromodel, extra) are absent from the TZ. Recorded in src/features/catalog/categories.ts as apiType, where null means 'no such type in the DB yet'.

nodes.label: Home Feed Response Shape
nodes.rationale: One response carries the whole home screen; exactly one of banners/content/categories/creators is filled per section type. Card fields in src/features/home/types.ts mirror HomeFeedDto.java. Empty sections are omitted. Cards carry accessPolicy but no price, so posters show a policy badge rather than an amount.

nodes.label: Lazily Created Homepage Sections
nodes.rationale: Home rows are created lazily on the first admin call to GET /api/v1/app/admin/homepage/sections, so on a clean database /api/v1/app/home honestly returns sections: [] and the app shows an empty state. Verified locally: 0 sections before the admin call, 12 after.

nodes.label: Media Namespace Separation
nodes.rationale: /api/v1/app/media/{id}/raw serves MediaAsset by numeric id, while /api/v1/file/getFile/{uuid} serves legacy casting attachments by UUID — a feed id used against the old endpoint returns 404. Images are open and cached; video checks entitlement and answers 404 (not 403) so existence stays hidden; Range is supported.

nodes.label: Watch Endpoint Client Contract
nodes.rationale: /watch/content/{id} returns 422 VALIDATION_ERROR for multi-episode content — the correct answer, not a failure — and the app uses that to switch to the episode list, because contentType and structureType are different axes (TZ §13/§14) and the feed card carries no structureType. sources[].url points at media/raw which re-checks rights, so the player is given an Authorization header via authHeaders() in src/lib/api.ts.

nodes.label: GET /app/content/{id}/episodes
nodes.rationale: Added in this work; without it series, mini-series and podcasts could not open at all. seasons is filled only for SEASONAL (no invented 'season 0' for EPISODIC), the server fixes the order, unpublished episodes are omitted and unpublished content returns 404 since 'exists but closed' would itself reveal existence. Deliberately contains no video URLs — otherwise the list alone would be enough to take a paid episode. Prices come from here, not from the feed.

nodes.label: Missing Mobile Endpoints
nodes.rationale: No catalog/search, content page, purchases or payments (Click/Payme/Uzum/UZCARD/Visa/MC), casting announcements (absent from both old and new API), chats, balance/payout history, Creator Studio 50/50, in-app Premium, or push. src/lib/placeholder.ts survives only for casting announcements and client prices; premieres were removed once the home feed went live.

nodes.label: UzCasting Logo System
nodes.rationale: Sources in assets/brand (logo.svg 512x512 viewBox, logo-source.png 4096x4096). Mark is a UZ monogram with a play triangle and film strip; gradient #6F20FF -> #A72DFF -> #E33CFF matching the TZ Neon Purple / Magenta.

nodes.label: Vector Where Possible, Raster Only Where Forced
nodes.rationale: SVG inside the app via react-native-svg-transformer: any size without blur, 5 KB instead of 1.9 MB, gradient stays live. PNG only for what the OS renders (app icon, splash), because Android/iOS accept raster only.
nodes.norm_label: vector where possible, raster only where forced

nodes.label: Platform Icon Constraints
nodes.rationale: iOS icons must not be transparent; the Android adaptive-icon safe zone is ~66% of the side, so the foreground logo is scaled to 62% or the mask clips it. Icons are regenerated by script with transparent-edge trimming rather than resized by hand.

nodes.label: Three OAuth Clients Requirement
nodes.rationale: Android (package + SHA-1), iOS (bundle ID) and Web (origins + redirect URIs) clients are all needed; a single Web client cannot serve a mobile app. A custom scheme like uzcasting:// is rejected by the Web client's redirect URIs — native client types exist precisely because their redirect is derived from the package/bundle ID.

nodes.label: Shared Debug Keystore For EAS
nodes.rationale: EAS would otherwise generate its own keystore, producing a second SHA-1 that would have to be added to the Android client; instead the debug keystore is copied into mobile/credentials and wired via credentials.json with credentialsSource: local. The release SHA-1 (or the Play App Signing re-issued key) must be added before production login works.

nodes.label: Dual URL Scheme In app.json
nodes.rationale: expo-auth-session builds a native redirect of uz.uzcasting.app:/oauthredirect, which is not the primary 'uzcasting' scheme, so both are registered; without the second the browser could not return to the app after consent and login would hang on a blank tab. For web preview, Google additionally requires the exact origin (e.g. http://localhost:8082) or it returns redirect_uri_mismatch.

nodes.label: app.google.client-ids Server Property
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/auth/google validates the ID token against an allowlist of client IDs and deliberately answers 503 when the list is missing rather than accepting any token. All client IDs must be listed because each platform's token carries its own aud.

nodes.label: Google Login Deploy Blockers
nodes.rationale: Remaining blockers are the backend deploy and then the client-ids property, in that order. A curl probe distinguishes them: 405 means the old build is deployed (Spring Boot's static handler answers GET-only on /**), 503 means the property is unset, 401 means everything is configured.

nodes.label: expo-auth-session Over Native SDK
nodes.rationale: Browser OAuth with no native modules was chosen because it needs nothing but a client ID and can later be swapped for @react-native-google-signin without rewriting screens — everything is hidden behind GoogleSignInButton. Two traps hit already: Google.useIdTokenAuthRequest throws without a client ID (hooks cannot be called conditionally, so the button mounts only when keys exist), and the import path must be lowercase 'google' or Metro fails on non-Windows filesystems.

nodes.label: .env Does Not Reach EAS Builds
nodes.rationale: EAS uploads only git-tracked files and .env is gitignored, so every EXPO_PUBLIC_* would be undefined in the APK with no build error — visible only on the phone. Client IDs are therefore duplicated into eas.json env for the development and preview profiles (no secrets: a client ID ships inside the APK anyway). eas.json also rejects '//' comment keys.

nodes.label: Phone-Or-Google Auth Flow
nodes.rationale: Agreed with the client: sign in by phone OR Google. Requiring a phone after Google turned out to be our own invention, not a TZ requirement, so the backend's phone_required is now a hint that the account has no number rather than a block; the number is requested only where it is genuinely needed (creator payouts, phone-bound payment systems). The (auth)/phone-link screen remains but is opened on demand with a 'later' option.

nodes.label: Spring local Profile
nodes.rationale: In-memory H2 in PostgreSQL mode, no Postgres and no password, port 8080 bound to 0.0.0.0 so the phone can reach it, Google client-ids preset. The database lives only while the process runs — every start is a clean seed, deliberately, so no junk accumulates. Must be launched from the repo root because AttachmentServiceImpl resolves files relative to backend/files.

nodes.label: LocalSeeder Test Data
nodes.rationale: Runs only when app.local.seed=true, a property present only in the local profile, so it cannot fire on the server by accident. Phones, emails and measurements are left empty on purpose because on the live API those are PII served without authorisation. Photos are generated on the fly with deterministic names so reruns reuse the same files.

nodes.label: LAN IP In EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL
nodes.rationale: The phone must target the computer's LAN IP, not localhost. EXPO_PUBLIC_* are inlined into the bundle at build time, so editing .env without restarting Metro changes nothing — the most common cause of 'the app loads no data' is a stale IP after a Wi-Fi change.

nodes.label: Dev Firewall Exposure
nodes.rationale: Inbound 8080 (backend) and 8081 (Metro) are opened for the Private profile only. Because SecurityConfig lets anyone in, the local backend is visible to everyone on a shared network — the data is fake and in-memory, but the rules should be removed after work.

nodes.label: H2 Console And open-in-view Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: spring.h2.console.enabled=true adds a servlet after which Spring Security cannot decide whether the SecurityConfig patterns are Spring MVC patterns and startup fails, so the console is off. open-in-view=false breaks /casting-user/web because CastingUser.photos is lazy and serialised outside the transaction (500) — meaning the production backend depends on that setting too, and it must be changed together with the backend developer.

nodes.label: Four Revenue Streams
nodes.rationale: Episode -> Premiere -> Premium -> Stars. The client's intent is not to tie users to one subscription but to let them pick a convenient level; this closes open question #1 (subscription vs per-item) with 'both, plus an intermediate level'. The 13.08.2026 client message overrides conflicting TZ figures.

nodes.label: Single Episode Purchase (3 000 UZS)
nodes.rationale: Price lowered from the TZ's 5 000 to 3 000; the V4 mockups and all four PDFs still show 5 000 and are outdated. Only the selected episode unlocks.

nodes.label: Premiere Purchase (15 000 UZS)
nodes.rationale: A new tier absent from the TZ, giving access to all episodes of one series/premiere. The client's wording says 'existing episodes'; whether it covers episodes released later is an open question.

nodes.label: UzCasting Premium Subscription
nodes.rationale: 1/3/6/12 months at 24 000 / 49 999 / 99 000 / 159 900 UZS, the yearly plan flagged as the best value. 'Ad-free viewing' implies non-Premium users see ads — an entire advertising subsystem the TZ never mentions.

nodes.label: UzCasting Stars Donations
nodes.rationale: Internal virtual currency in packs of 10/50/100/500/1000, shown on the creator profile. A second client message extends it to films, a leaderboard, and a monthly awards ceremony — making Stars a ranking mechanic, not just donations, and an entirely new subsystem with no TZ coverage. The Stars-to-UZS rate is still unspecified.

nodes.label: Single Backend Entitlement Check
nodes.rationale: With four possible entitlement sources (episode purchase, premiere purchase, active subscription, free content) the 'can this be watched' check must live in one place on the backend and not be smeared across the client. Requires entities Purchase, Subscription, Entitlement, StarsBalance, StarsTransaction, StarsLeaderboard.

nodes.label: Store Billing Compliance Risk
nodes.rationale: Episodes, premiere access, subscription and Stars are all in-app digital content, which Google Play and Apple require to be sold through their billing at 15-30% commission; Click/Payme/Uzum/UZCARD for such goods violates store rules and gets the app pulled. The commission is taken before the 50/50 creator split (a 3 000 UZS episode yields the creator ~1 050-1 275, not 1 500), Stars are the most tightly regulated category, and the common workaround is selling only on the website with no purchase buttons in the app.

nodes.label: Read Versioned Expo Docs First
nodes.rationale: Expo has changed; agents must read the exact versioned docs at docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0 before writing any code, rather than relying on remembered APIs.

nodes.label: mobile CLAUDE.md AGENTS Import
nodes.rationale: A one-line file whose entire content is @AGENTS.md, so the mobile Claude instructions are a single source of truth shared with other agent tools.

nodes.label: Bundled SPA Shell (backend static)
nodes.rationale: The built CRA bundle (main.4a14df90.js / main.40ff7fb6.css) copied into Spring Boot's static resources, titled 'Uzcasting'. Because Spring serves it for unknown paths, API calls to routes the deployed build lacks come back as 200 HTML instead of 404.

nodes.label: Console Output Suppression
nodes.rationale: An inline script stubs console.log/error/warn to no-ops inside #root, silencing all browser diagnostics in production — which also hides genuine runtime errors from anyone debugging the deployed site.

nodes.label: Runtime CDN Asset Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Tailwind is loaded at runtime from jsdelivr (@tailwindcss/browser@4) rather than compiled at build time, plus Font Awesome 6.7 from cdnjs (SRI-pinned) and the Urbanist family from Google Fonts — so styling depends on three third-party hosts being reachable.

nodes.label: CRA index.html Template
nodes.rationale: Source template using %PUBLIC_URL% placeholders that produces the backend's static index.html at build time; carries the same CDN Tailwind/Font Awesome/Urbanist links and the same console-suppression script.

nodes.label: Create React App Scripts
nodes.rationale: Untouched CRA boilerplate documenting npm start/test/build/eject; the project's real frontend instructions live in the root README instead.

nodes.label: Open Crawl robots.txt (backend static)
nodes.rationale: Default CRA robots.txt with an empty Disallow, allowing every crawler everywhere — including, given the permitAll SecurityConfig, publicly reachable API paths.

nodes.label: Open Crawl robots.txt (frontend public)
nodes.rationale: Source of the deployed robots.txt; unchanged CRA default with User-agent: * and an empty Disallow.

nodes.label: Bundled OSS License Manifest
nodes.rationale: Webpack-extracted license banners revealing the production bundle's stack: React + react-dom + scheduler, classnames, and React Router / @remix-run/router v6.23.1 — all MIT.

nodes.label: Effective Keyframe Inventory
nodes.rationale: Flattened list of every @keyframes reaching the page, including third-party ones (react-responsive-modal overlay/modal in-out) alongside the project's own; used to audit animation collisions.

nodes.label: Project Keyframe Inventory
nodes.rationale: Alphabetised subset authored by the project (fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideIn, slideDown, menuSlideIn, cardEnter, modalIn, shake, shineEffect, colorShift/colorShiftDark, pulseAnimation, float, bbl, headerScroll…), with a blue/indigo #3b82f6-#312e81 motion palette.

nodes.label: UzCasting Mobile Platform
nodes.rationale: Three products fused in one app (casting portfolio, paid premieres, creator economy) because the monetization loop needs creators, content and buyers on the same surface.

nodes.label: Monetization Core Flow (free episode 1 to paid continuation)
nodes.rationale: Blogger posts episode 1 free on YouTube/Instagram, CTA sends viewers to UzCasting to buy the continuation; payment confirmed -> entitlement -> protected player; 50/50 revenue share. Everything else in the app is scaffolding around this single scenario.
nodes.norm_label: monetization core flow (free episode 1 to paid continuation)

nodes.label: Mobile Design System Palette
nodes.rationale: Seven HEX tokens are fixed by the client spec (V2 p.18) and may not change; six derived neutral/status tokens were added by the team because the eight mandatory states cannot be built without them. Source of truth is tailwind.config.js plus src/theme/tokens.ts, both must be edited together.

nodes.label: Eight Mandatory UI States
nodes.rationale: loading/empty/error/success/locked/purchased/disabled/offline required on every screen; implementation split across ScreenState, Button and Badge so a screen is not 'done' until all applicable states are covered.

nodes.label: Five Tab Navigation (Bosh sahifa/Casting/Premyera/Xabarlar/Profil)
nodes.rationale: Tab composition comes from the client spec, not from Yangi.TV; Creator Studio is a section inside Profil rather than a sixth tab so the bar matches the approved mockups.

nodes.label: Ten Creator Directions
nodes.rationale: V3 only details catalogs for 7 of the 10; Styling and Courses have no screens, and the backend only has 4 of the 10 casting types, so 6 directions honestly render an empty state.

nodes.label: Mobile Tech Stack (Expo SDK 57)
nodes.rationale: expo-router, NativeWind+Tailwind (shares the palette config with the web frontend), TanStack Query for server state, Zustand for client state, axios for token interceptors, expo-web-browser + uzcasting:// deeplink because Click/Payme/Uzum ship no native RN SDKs.

nodes.label: Expo Router / NativeWind Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: From SDK 56 expo-router is incompatible with direct @react-navigation imports; babel-preset-expo must be in devDependencies for NativeWind; app.json scheme uzcasting is required for return from the payment webview; lib/api.ts must attach the Authorization header or paid content and the player return 404.

nodes.label: Phone-OTP or Google Sign-In (interchangeable)
nodes.rationale: Phone is not requested after Google because the spec explicitly allows an email account and names social login as optional; the number is collected later, where payouts and payments actually need it. Requires three Google OAuth clients (Android, iOS, Web).

nodes.label: Server-Driven Home Feed (GET /api/v1/app/home)
nodes.rationale: Home is an array of typed blocks assembled by the server; otherwise every storefront change would need a store release.

nodes.label: Watch Entitlement API (/api/v1/app/watch/**)
nodes.rationale: Access right, reason and price all come from the server, never decided client-side.

nodes.label: contentType is not structureType
nodes.rationale: Type (serial, show) cannot tell whether content is whole or episodic - they are different axes of the spec; the client only learns the structure from the /watch response.

nodes.label: Mobile Work Stages 0-4
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 (design) blocks development because the spec states Figma is the final source of truth; stage 3 is Android+UZ/RU, stage 4 iOS+EN.

nodes.label: Open Questions to the Client (mobile)
nodes.rationale: Styling/Courses catalogs, Latin vs Cyrillic Uzbek, refund rules, DRM vs signed URLs, and who grants the verified badge remain unanswered; the episode price was cut from 5000 to 3000 on 13.08.2026.

nodes.norm_label: v4 mockups are not a layout reference

nodes.label: Yangi.TV Structural Analysis
nodes.rationale: Yangi.TV is a plain OTT cinema with time-based subscriptions and no casting/portfolio/creator economy, so it supplies structure for only the content half of UzCasting; its red/black palette is explicitly not taken.

nodes.label: Floating Capsule TabBar
nodes.rationale: Shape borrowed from Yangi.TV, colors from the spec: active tab is Neon Purple with a weak 18% glow because the spec asks for glow 'in moderation'. Because the bar floats, screens get bottom padding via useTabBarHeight().

nodes.label: Content Detail Screen Template
nodes.rationale: The densest Yangi.TV screen; its 11-block structure is copied almost wholesale and reused for both premiere detail and creator profile.

nodes.label: Tariff Card Template
nodes.rationale: Cannot be copied for UzCasting: it sells catalog access for a period, whereas UzCasting sells one episode forever.

nodes.label: Subscription vs Per-Episode Purchase Divergence
nodes.rationale: The most important conclusion of the Yangi.TV analysis: Yangi.TV badges are PREMIUM/Bepul while UzCasting badges are locked/purchased; the spec carries both a per-episode price and a Premium subscription without describing how they combine, so the payment screen is not designed until the client answers.

nodes.label: Payment Method Grid
nodes.rationale: The one purchase-flow element safe to copy now: it is identical for both monetization models and matches the spec's provider list (Click, Payme, Uzum, UZCARD, Visa, Mastercard).

nodes.label: First Launch Flow (Splash to Onboarding to Kirish)
nodes.rationale: Client-supplied mockup of 14.08.2026 is the layout source of truth for S01/S02/S03 and outranks earlier team decisions; the 'seen onboarding' flag lives in SecureStore.
nodes.norm_label: first launch flow (splash to onboarding to kirish)

nodes.label: Splash as Overlay, Not Route
nodes.rationale: A splash route would claim '/' which already belongs to (tabs)/index, and would stay in history so Back from login would return to it; instead it sits above the navigator and is removed once the destination is decided.

nodes.label: UzCasting Screen Map
nodes.rationale: Yangi.TV structure overlaid onto the spec's entities: Casting replaces To'plam, Premyera and Xabarlar have no Yangi.TV analogue.

nodes.label: Derived Component Inventory
nodes.rationale: MetaTable, StatChips, PersonAvatar, PaymentMethodGrid and BottomSheet remain unbuilt because they all belong to screens blocked on monetization answers.

nodes.label: Trilingual Language Switcher (UZ/RU/EN)
nodes.rationale: English was moved to the first release at the client's request although the spec put it in stage 2; the choice is applied before the splash is removed, otherwise the first screen flashes Uzbek. Key sets in all three locale files must match. Storage is a SecureStore wrapper with a localStorage fallback for web, but tokens never go through it - they need Keystore/Keychain.

nodes.label: Registration Screen Analysis (one screen, one action)
nodes.rationale: Phone field with +998 prefix, consent links, one DAVOM ETISH button and nothing else; requiring a phone number right after Google was a self-invented barrier based on a misread spec reference.
nodes.norm_label: registration screen analysis (one screen, one action)

nodes.label: UzCasting Backend Architecture
nodes.rationale: Spring Boot 3.1.2 / Java 17 / Maven / PostgreSQL layered monolith; the frontend build is packed into the fat jar so one artifact serves the whole site. Must be started from the repo root because Attachment writes to the relative path backend/files/.

nodes.label: Layered Monolith (Controller-Service-Repository)
nodes.rationale: Capitalised package names are non-standard but consistent, so they are kept; new PHASE 3+ modules follow the same convention.

nodes.label: JWT Authentication (typed access/refresh tokens)
nodes.rationale: A typ claim separates access from refresh because previously both were identical and a stolen refresh token opened the entire API; access life was cut from 100 to 15 minutes.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Rotation and Revocation
nodes.rationale: refresh_token table (V25) stores only the jti, never the token text; each refresh revokes the previous one and a replayed revoked token is treated as theft, closing the user's whole chain. Delivered as an httpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict cookie, never in the response body.

nodes.label: LoginAttemptService (per-account lockout)
nodes.rationale: Five failures lock an account for 15 minutes; IP-level throttling is a separate RateLimitFilter so the two cannot mask each other.

nodes.label: PlatformRole Hierarchy (HYPER_ADMIN to USER)
nodes.rationale: Higher roles inherit lower rights; WORKER is governed by fine-grained Permissions; staff creation is checked at the endpoint so privilege escalation is impossible. Hiding a frontend menu is not security - every endpoint checks independently. The legacy UserRoles enum is preserved (production rows exist) and mapped via RoleMapper.

nodes.label: StorageService Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Local/Timeweb/S3 implementations behind one interface so the provider name never leaks into business logic; uploads stream via Files.copy so large video never loads fully into RAM. Extension allowlist, fully server-side file names, and normalize()+startsWith(ROOT) checks on both write and read.

nodes.label: MediaAsset Entity
nodes.rationale: New entity added instead of touching the legacy Attachment, which is still live in the Telegram bot flow.

nodes.label: CMS Content Model (Content/Season/Episode/EpisodeVideo)
nodes.rationale: Lives in a separate Cms.* package so it never mixes with the legacy Entity/Repository (D16), and must be listed in @EntityScan/@EnableJpaRepositories or the repositories are not found. There is deliberately no single episode.videoUrl field - an EpisodeVideo list supports multiple parts and dubbing languages. @Version detects two admins editing at once, deletedAt gives soft delete, prices are BigDecimal, list queries use @EntityGraph against N+1.

nodes.label: Separate Translation Tables (not JSON columns)
nodes.rationale: Text goes into per-parent tables with UNIQUE(parent_id, locale) rather than a JSON column because search and indexing must work per language. Media locale is optional: NULL means all languages, an explicit locale wins when present, so a per-language poster is possible but not mandatory.

nodes.label: AccessPolicy (FREE/PREMIUM_ONLY/PURCHASE_ONLY/PREMIUM_OR_PURCHASE)
nodes.rationale: Entitlement can arrive from four sources - single episode purchase (default 3000 sum stored in the DB, not hardcoded), whole-premiere purchase, an active Premium subscription, or free content. Casting projects are covered by Premium but never by one-off purchase.

nodes.label: AccessService.canWatch (single access gate)
nodes.rationale: One entry point so the rule is never scattered across the client or several services; the lock in the episode list and the lock on the watch page derive from the same call and therefore cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: UserBalance (money, Stars, Coins)
nodes.rationale: Exchange rates and packages are admin-managed settings rather than code constants.

nodes.label: DonationTransaction (immutable)
nodes.rationale: No hard delete; donations are accounted separately per content and per creator.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Analytics Model (raw events to daily aggregates)
nodes.rationale: The dashboard never runs COUNT(*) over millions of raw events; when there is no data it shows an empty state rather than a fabricated number.
nodes.norm_label: two-layer analytics model (raw events to daily aggregates)

nodes.label: AuditLog
nodes.rationale: Records actor, action, entity, before/after, ip and user agent; passwords, tokens and payment credentials are never written, and a plain Admin cannot delete audit rows.

nodes.label: Flyway Migration Plan (baseline-on-migrate)
nodes.rationale: V1__baseline.sql records the existing schema; ddl-auto only moves from update to validate after the baseline is verified in production.

nodes.label: Asia/Tashkent Timezone Setting
nodes.rationale: Over 310 LocalDateTime uses carry no zone, so without app.timezone the container's UTC made a scheduled premiere publish five hours late.

nodes.label: Per-Entity ID Strategy
nodes.rationale: Existing entities keep their id types (User UUID, CastingUser Integer, Role manual int as technical debt) because production rows exist; all new entities use Long + IDENTITY.

nodes.label: Backend Roadmap Checklist
nodes.rationale: Status is verified from code, not assumed: every [x] is backed by a working endpoint or a passing test. 294 tests, 15 migrations, 49 entities, 15 services, 83 admin endpoints.

nodes.label: Permission Enum (43 permissions, 13 modules)
nodes.rationale: Permissions are never written into the token - they are read from the database on every request, so revoking one weakens the existing token immediately.

nodes.label: @RequirePermission / PermissionAspect / PermissionInterceptor
nodes.rationale: The interceptor runs before request-body validation (bug B16), and AdminEndpointGuardTest makes it impossible to add an unguarded admin endpoint.

nodes.label: OldCastingFrozenTest
nodes.rationale: Freezes the legacy casting paths, controllers, entities, table names and repositories so the working production flow cannot be renamed away.

nodes.label: ExistingCastingRegressionTest
nodes.rationale: The more important of the two guards: the route can stay in place while the internal logic breaks, so this test exercises the application, accept/reject and bot message behaviour itself.

nodes.label: /api/v1/app/** API Namespace
nodes.rationale: The legacy /api/v1/** namespace is frozen and the new platform is versioned beside it; /content/{id}/episodes deliberately returns no video link - that only comes from /watch/{episodeId} after the right is confirmed.

nodes.label: OTP Login (unwritten)
nodes.rationale: Spec R14 requires a 4-6 digit code, 5-minute life, 60s resend and a 15-minute block after 3 errors - none of it exists; app users still sign in through the legacy /api/v1/auth/login, which must keep working until clients migrate.

nodes.label: Missing Client-Facing APIs
nodes.rationale: catalog, content page, search, comments, ads, me, purchases and OTP auth are unopened, so the mobile app currently cannot reach the new content at all; a content card endpoint is missing, so a direct deep link finds an empty home cache.

nodes.label: Backend Next Steps by Impact
nodes.rationale: Ordered by impact: client APIs, payments (blocked on store billing risk), FCM, refresh token store, device limit, OpenAPI, and the Bunny Stream video hosting decision that contradicts the current local-storage plus Range solution.

nodes.label: Soft Delete Strategy
nodes.rationale: Two strategies by entity type, with deliberate hard-delete exceptions and a guard test; a disappearing row is not merely absent data but broken history.

nodes.label: 27 Unindexed Foreign Keys Found
nodes.rationale: Audit of database rules also found five translation tables whose unique constraint column order was reversed, which defeated the intended lookups.

nodes.label: N+1 Fix That Created Its Own N+1
nodes.rationale: The first correction introduced a new N+1 and, in the first review, lost data; documented as a warning against blind batching.
nodes.norm_label: n+1 fix that created its own n+1

nodes.label: 2FA Deliberately Not Implemented
nodes.rationale: The channel (SMS, TOTP or email) has not been chosen by the client; the architecture is ready but writing it now would guess the channel, and the same blocker also holds up self-service password reset.

nodes.label: UzCasting Admin Panel Frontend Architecture
nodes.rationale: React 18.3.1 on CRA 5 in plain JavaScript; npm install needs --legacy-peer-deps because react-reveal, react-bootstrap-carousel and react-dice-roll do not declare React 18 support. The build output is copied into the backend static folder so one jar serves everything.

nodes.label: src/adminpanel Module
nodes.rationale: New panel routes live under /app/panel/* in adminpanel/routes.jsx so App.js does not keep growing - exactly one line was added to App.js. The legacy admin/, bot-admin/ and pages/ trees are untouched. Three pages were split into their own folders once a page grew several independent modals; the split boundary is 'does the modal load its own data'.

nodes.label: AuthContext with In-Memory Access Token
nodes.rationale: Storing the access token in localStorage let any script on the page read it and turned one XSS into long-lived access, so it now lives in memory while the refresh token sits in an httpOnly cookie JavaScript cannot see. On reload the session is restored via POST /auth/refresh and the profile re-fetched from /auth/me because role or permissions may have changed; only the non-secret profile stays in localStorage, purely to paint the menu immediately.

nodes.label: api/client.js with Single-Flight Refresh
nodes.rationale: On 401 it refreshes once and replays the request; concurrent requests share one refresh, otherwise each would start its own rotation, revoke the others' token and eject the user with a 'theft detected' reason.

nodes.label: useApi Hook
nodes.rationale: Minimal loading/error/reload hook with no cache; pages depend on it so that adding TanStack Query later swaps only this hook and leaves pages unchanged.

nodes.label: PermissionGuard and Filtered Sidebar
nodes.rationale: Frontend guarding is UX only - hiding a menu is not security; verified in the browser that a WORKER hitting /app/panel/staff still gets 403 ACCESS_DENIED from the backend.

nodes.label: Dark Blue Panel Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: Client decision of 19.08.2026: the admin panel is a separate product surface in dark blue, deliberately not the mobile app's approved purple/black palette, so there is no conflict. Hex values exist only in theme/panel.css.

nodes.label: Three CSS Conflicts with the Legacy Site
nodes.rationale: A global `* { font-family: Lora !important }` bleeds site-wide; panel classes tie with Tailwind utilities on specificity so Tailwind classes like lg:hidden are banned inside the panel in favour of its own media queries; Chrome autofill whitening is overridden with an inset shadow.
nodes.norm_label: three css conflicts with the legacy site

nodes.label: Fresh-Mount Modal Pattern
nodes.rationale: Modals are conditionally rendered rather than always mounted and hidden with `open`, because otherwise reopening carried stale state - previous text in the password dialog, another employee's checkboxes in the permissions dialog, an outdated 'where used' list in the media dialog.

nodes.label: TrendChart (inline SVG)
nodes.rationale: No charting library was added - inline SVG driven by a series prop is enough.

nodes.label: ContentEditor (six sections, not one 100-input form)
nodes.rationale: Basics, texts (UZ/RU/EN tabs marking unfilled languages), media including per-language posters, creators, monetization and publication; unsaved-change warning, and PUBLISHED cannot be selected without CONTENT_PUBLISH.

nodes.label: EpisodesTab (adapts to content structure)
nodes.rationale: SEASONAL shows seasons with nested episodes, EPISODIC a flat list, SINGLE hides the section entirely; no modal inside a modal - the list and form swap with a back button - and no second Save button, to avoid confusion. Inherited access policy is shown explicitly.

nodes.label: Chunked Video Upload
nodes.rationale: Large videos are uploaded in retryable chunks through the project's own server - the approach the Bunny Stream documents later contradict.

nodes.label: Stage F1 - Staff Management
nodes.rationale: Only roles below the actor's own are visible (filtered on the backend), role choice in the create form is limited by the creator's rights, and every dangerous action is behind a confirmation dialog.

nodes.label: Stage F3 - Dashboard Charts and Tables
nodes.rationale: A single dashboard/summary call feeds ten real metrics; modules that do not exist yet render an explicit dash instead of a fake chart.
nodes.norm_label: stage f3 - dashboard charts and tables

nodes.label: Stage F4 - Homepage Ordering and Manual Selection
nodes.rationale: 12 sections with in-list toggles, ordering and manual content picking; all three translations are shown in a column with a red dash where one is missing.
nodes.norm_label: stage f4 - homepage ordering and manual selection

nodes.label: Stage F5 - Reports
nodes.rationale: Ad, content and notification report modals; the backend already supported five object filters combined with the period, but the panel only offered period buttons, so 'this category, last 7 days' could not be asked at all.

nodes.label: B4 - Frontend Admin Guard Never Ran
nodes.rationale: App.js listed blockedPages = ['/dashboard'] but no such route exists - the real admin routes are /aadmin/*, so checkSecurity() never fired and admin pages were unguarded on the frontend.
nodes.norm_label: b4 - frontend admin guard never ran

nodes.label: 38 Critical Flow Tests
nodes.rationale: They guard behaviours that break silently: slug not changing on edit, genres and creators surviving a save, version being sent, automatic episode numbering, accessPolicyOverride going null when inherited, and premiere fields not leaking into the ad request.

nodes.label: Generic DataTable Deliberately Not Built
nodes.rationale: Columns and filters differ too much between pages, so shared TableWrap/Pagination/SearchInput primitives were kept while a universal DataTable and FilterPanel were skipped to avoid over-abstraction.

nodes.label: TZ Checklist §6-§98
nodes.rationale: 92 sections, not 93 - the spec has no §81. Final count 75 complete, 14 partial, 3 open. §0-§5 and §100-§110 are working rules, not tasks, and are excluded from the count.

nodes.label: Roadmap Documents Were Stale - Four Corrections
nodes.rationale: Checking the code showed BACKEND_ROADMAP.md lagged reality and wrongly reported §92 secrets, §61 refresh tokens, §64 OpenAPI and §47/§86 as open when they were already done - the reason this checklist is code-verified rather than document-derived.
nodes.norm_label: roadmap documents were stale - four corrections

nodes.label: Blocker - Payment Provider Merchant Data (§44)
nodes.rationale: Payme/Click/Uzum merchant credentials never arrived, so there is no real integration; the exchange rate is also unstated, which is why panel prices show 0 meaning 'not configured' rather than an estimate.

nodes.label: Blocker - FCM Credentials (§32)
nodes.rationale: Notifications are stored and scheduled but never delivered; the panel states this in a yellow warning, and delivered/sent counts read 'not measured' rather than zero, deliberately.

nodes.label: Blocker - 2FA Channel Choice (§63)
nodes.rationale: Choosing SMS, TOTP or email also unblocks the self-service password reset in §61.

nodes.label: Blocker - Stars and Coin Exchange Rate (§40, §41)
nodes.rationale: Without a rate donations cannot be valued in money and currency package prices stay at 0.
nodes.norm_label: blocker - stars and coin exchange rate (§40, §41)

nodes.label: Build Environment Problem (JDK 25 breaks Lombok)
nodes.rationale: Only JDK 25 is installed, mvnw is broken, and from JDK 23 javac disables annotation processors by default while maven-compiler-plugin is pinned at 3.11.0 - Lombok stops working and 410 'cannot find symbol' errors appear. Backend work was halted rather than committing unverifiable changes; the fix is JDK 17/21 or plugin 3.13+ with explicit annotationProcessorPaths.

nodes.label: Modal Focus-Loss Bug (one character per field)
nodes.rationale: The Modal effect depended on onClose, which parents recreate every render, so every keystroke re-ran the effect and moved focus to the first element - only one character could be typed. Fixed by holding onClose in a ref so the effect depends only on `open`. A second test-found bug: an unguarded replace() on a missing effectiveAccessPolicy whited out the whole seasons/episodes section.
nodes.norm_label: modal focus-loss bug (one character per field)

nodes.label: UzCasting Admin Web Platform Master Development Prompt
nodes.rationale: The client's own technical specification. §0 forbids starting with code: audit and roadmap documents come first, and the three roadmap files have a mandatory format.

nodes.norm_label: §6-§10 role hierarchy (hyper_admin, super_admin, admin, worker, user)

nodes.label: §11 Backend Authorization - Two Layers
nodes.rationale: Role plus permission checked on the backend on every request, read from the database rather than from the token; the spec marks this as especially important because a hidden menu is not protection.

nodes.label: §13 Content Platform - Three Independent Axes
nodes.rationale: Content type, structure and format are separate dimensions; type, category and genre are not the same thing.

nodes.rationale: Four distinct concepts that must not substitute for one another.

nodes.label: §23 Content Access Model (FREE, PREMIUM, PURCHASE, inheritance)

nodes.label: §26 Media Library
nodes.rationale: List, search, filter, where-used tracking, archive, restore and delete.

nodes.label: §27-§29 Advertisement Module and Analytics
nodes.rationale: Image plus mobileImage, time window, audience, internal/external link types, and per-ad impressions, clicks, uniques, CTR and daily breakdown.

nodes.label: §32-§33 Notifications and Notification Report

nodes.label: §36-§38 Premium Tariffs, Rights and Gifting

nodes.label: §50-§51 Brand, Design Tokens and UI Requirements
nodes.rationale: Hex values confined to one theme file; every list page must have search, filter, pagination, sorting, loading, empty, error and retry.

nodes.rationale: Errors appear next to the field; the audit found nine dead validation annotations that never ran.

nodes.rationale: All project documents were gathered into /roadmap/ by client decision even though the spec asked for them in the root, backend/ and frontend/; the BACKEND_/FRONTEND_ prefixes exist because both architecture files would otherwise share a name. If the old Miro spec conflicts with this file, this file wins.

nodes.label: Scope Exclusion - Social Network, Messenger, Friends, Feed
nodes.rationale: The old spec carried a social-network/messenger concept that was not accepted as a core task; verified that no such feature exists in Cms/, Admin/ or src/adminpanel/.

nodes.label: Trap - the Message Entity Is Not a Messenger
nodes.rationale: The name invites deleting it as messenger leftovers, but it is the accept/reject reply the Telegram bot delivers to a casting applicant; deleting it means candidates never hear back, so a dedicated test guards it.
nodes.norm_label: trap - the message entity is not a messenger

nodes.label: Three-Axis Content Classification (type, category, genre)
nodes.rationale: Separated at all three layers - database, API and panel - and guarded by ContentClassificationTest, because the likeliest silent failure is someone folding category into the type enum, after which a podcast in the drama genre becomes inexpressible. The dev seeder had exactly that mistake: content types seeded as categories.

nodes.label: Bunny Stream Decision Pending
nodes.rationale: The client added two Bunny documents on 21.08.2026 that define a fundamentally different video architecture - direct TUS upload to Bunny and signed HLS from Bunny CDN - contradicting the built local storage with chunked upload and Range responses. They also assume a different stack (Java 21, Gradle, uz.streaming, Vite). No video code changes until the client decides.

nodes.label: Architecture Decisions D1-D26
nodes.rationale: Keep existing folders and stack, stay in JavaScript, introduce Flyway with baseline-on-migrate, money as BigDecimal, per-entity ID strategy, separate translation tables over JSON columns, optional per-locale media, dark blue panel vs spec palette for mobile, H2 file DB for dev, no enum check constraints in migrations, homepage assembled from cms_homepage_section, prices and rates in cms_platform_setting, and inline SVG instead of a chart library.

nodes.label: Trilingual Architecture (UZ/RU/EN mandatory)
nodes.rationale: Client requirement that all content and menus exist in three languages, with some images uploaded specifically per language.

nodes.label: B1 - Entire API Was permitAll
nodes.rationale: SecurityConfig granted permitAll on every method and path, so DELETE and admin endpoints were open without a token and the written JWT filter had nothing to enforce.

nodes.label: B2 - Public Endpoint Returned Personal Data
nodes.rationale: The open catalog returned phone, email, exact birth date and body measurements, including profiles of minors - a legal risk rather than technical debt, fixed with a showcase DTO.
nodes.norm_label: b2 - public endpoint returned personal data

nodes.label: B3 - Secrets in the Repository
nodes.rationale: Database password and JWT key were in code; resolved by gitignoring application.properties, shipping only an .example, and removing the JWT default.

nodes.label: B15 - Paid Video Was Publicly Reachable
nodes.rationale: Media raw access served video without an entitlement check; images stay public while video now requires the right.
nodes.norm_label: b15 - paid video was publicly reachable

nodes.label: Dev Environment and Seeded Entitlement Accounts
nodes.rationale: Backend must be launched from the repository root because file paths are relative; seeded app users cover the different entitlement states so access rules can be exercised without payments.
nodes.norm_label: dev environment and seeded entitlement accounts

nodes.label: Future Mobile Scope (§14.2)
nodes.rationale: Watch later / saved items and other user-side mobile parts are recorded but deliberately not written now.

nodes.label: UzCasting Project Overview (one page)
nodes.rationale: Single-page summary of what the product is, where the code lives, what is ready and what is blocking; explicitly not a greenfield project - the casting half already runs in production with a backend, site, Telegram bot and admin panel.

nodes.label: Four-Level Monetization (episode, premiere, Premium, Stars)
nodes.rationale: The client's 13.08.2026 message overrides the spec's numbers: an episode is 3000 sum (not 5000), a whole premiere 15000, Premium runs 24000/49999/99000/159900 for 1/3/6/12 months, and Stars come in packages. Premium unlocks everything; per-episode and per-premiere purchases exist for people who will not subscribe. Premiere, Stars, rating and advertising appear nowhere in the spec - they all come from that message.

nodes.label: Three Blockers
nodes.rationale: Ordered by how badly each breaks the architecture or the economics: store billing, the unprotected API, and minors' personal data.

nodes.label: Store Billing Risk (15-30% commission)
nodes.rationale: Episodes, premieres, subscriptions and Stars are in-app digital content, so Google Play and the App Store require their own billing; using Click/Payme/Uzum for it breaks store rules and gets the app removed. The commission is taken before the 50/50 split, so on a 3000 sum episode the creator receives roughly 1050-1275 rather than 1500. Must be settled before the payment module is written.

nodes.label: Minors' Personal Data Legal Risk
nodes.rationale: The public endpoint returns phone, email, exact birth date and body measurements including profiles aged 17; the mobile app deliberately ignores those fields but the exposure is on the backend, making this a legal rather than technical problem.

nodes.label: Twelve Questions to the Client
nodes.rationale: Screens stay undesigned until these are answered: Stars pricing and whether Stars are creator income, whether a 15000 premiere covers future episodes, ad network, auto-renewal, 5000 vs 3000, Styling/Courses catalogs, 10 vs 4 categories actually present in the database, Latin vs Cyrillic, refund rules, DRM vs signed URLs, and verified badge criteria.

nodes.label: Data Source Status (real API vs placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Creators come from the real endpoint; premieres and casting announcements still come from src/lib/placeholder.ts and that file is deleted outright once the endpoints appear.
nodes.norm_label: data source status (real api vs placeholder)

nodes.label: Bunny Stream Streaming Service Project Context
nodes.rationale: Session-context document for a subscription video service for the Uzbek market where video lives in Bunny Stream and the backend only verifies rights and issues a temporary signed link.
nodes.norm_label: bunny stream streaming service project context

nodes.label: Server Is a Turnstile, Not a Pipe
nodes.rationale: Not a single byte of video passes through the VPS: upload goes straight from the admin panel to Bunny, playback straight from Bunny CDN to the device, and the backend only decides who may watch.
nodes.norm_label: server is a turnstile, not a pipe

nodes.label: Streaming Service Stack (Java 21, Gradle, Vite)
nodes.rationale: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 + PostgreSQL 16 + Flyway + Gradle Kotlin DSL, React Native/Expo mobile, React+Vite+Tailwind admin, packaged as catalog / playback / subscription / user / infrastructure modules under uz.streaming.

nodes.label: Bunny Stream (Video Library + CDN Pull Zone)
nodes.rationale: Handles transcoding into four qualities, HLS segmentation and regional replication; PostgreSQL stores metadata only and thumbnails are assembled from a URL template rather than stored.
nodes.norm_label: bunny stream (video library + cdn pull zone)

nodes.label: Directory Token Signing (isDirectory=true)
nodes.rationale: HLS is a manifest plus hundreds of segments, so a token signed for one file opens only the manifest while every segment returns 403; the token must be signed for the directory path and is then embedded in the URL path, not the query string.

nodes.label: No IP Binding on Signed URLs
nodes.rationale: A phone switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data changes IP mid-playback and would break it; account sharing is limited by an active-session counter instead.
nodes.norm_label: no ip binding on signed urls

nodes.label: Upload Signature SHA256(libraryId+apiKey+expiration+videoId)
nodes.rationale: Lifetime of at least one hour and preferably six, because large files upload slowly.

nodes.label: Bunny Webhook (unauthenticated)
nodes.rationale: It arrives with no authorization, so VideoLibraryId must be compared against ours and the handler must always answer 200 or Bunny keeps retrying.

nodes.label: TokenSigner from the Official BunnyCDN Repository
nodes.rationale: URL-signing cryptography is not to be hand-written; the official Java class is copied into infrastructure/bunny/.
nodes.norm_label: tokensigner from the official bunnycdn repository

nodes.label: No PATCH, DTO-Only Responses
nodes.rationale: Only GET/POST/PUT/DELETE; partial updates go through PUT with a full body, responses are Java records, errors flow through @RestControllerAdvice in a {code, message} shape, and JPA entities never leave a controller.

nodes.label: Secrets Only via Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: BUNNY_API_KEY, BUNNY_TOKEN_KEY, the JWT secret and the DB password appear in application.yml only as placeholders; direct video file links are never handed to a client, and access rights are checked on the backend.

nodes.label: Explicit Code/Developer Split and Stop Blocks
nodes.rationale: The developer is new to video streaming, so terms are explained inline, each step is marked CODE or DEVELOPER, and work halts with a STOP block whenever a dashboard action or environment variable is required; every step ends with a concrete way to verify it.
nodes.norm_label: explicit code/developer split and stop blocks

nodes.label: Bunny Stream Implementation Roadmap (Phases 0-8)
nodes.rationale: Strictly sequential phases, each step tagged as written by the agent or done by hand, and ticked off in the file itself.

nodes.label: Video Library Setup (Europe+Asia, 360p-1080p)
nodes.rationale: Europe and Asia replication is enough for Uzbekistan and 4K encoding is switched off.

nodes.label: Content Protection Settings (Block Direct URL, CDN Token Auth)
nodes.rationale: Direct Play is disabled so nothing can be played without a signed token.
nodes.norm_label: content protection settings (block direct url, cdn token auth)

nodes.label: Catalog Model (genres, series, seasons, episodes, videos)
nodes.rationale: videos carries bunny_video_id, status PROCESSING/READY/FAILED, required_plan and duration; covers are built from the CDN template and never stored in the database.
nodes.norm_label: catalog model (genres, series, seasons, episodes, videos)

nodes.label: Upload Ticket Endpoint (POST /api/admin/videos/upload-ticket)
nodes.rationale: Creates a PROCESSING row and returns the ids, expiration and signature the admin panel needs to TUS-upload the file straight to Bunny.

nodes.label: Bunny Webhook Handler (POST /api/webhooks/bunny)
nodes.rationale: Status 3 marks READY, status 5 FAILED, everything else is progress; the library id is verified and the endpoint always answers 200.

nodes.label: Subscription Plans (BASIC and PREMIUM with device limits)
nodes.rationale: BASIC allows 2 devices up to 720p, PREMIUM 4 devices at 1080p, matched against the video's required_plan.
nodes.norm_label: subscription plans (basic and premium with device limits)

nodes.label: DeviceSessionService (device limit with race protection)
nodes.rationale: Guards against several phones starting playback simultaneously and slipping past the limit.

nodes.label: Playback Check Order and Error Codes
nodes.rationale: Video READY, then subscription active, then plan covers, then device limit - returning 402 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED, 403 PLAN_TOO_LOW, 409 DEVICE_LIMIT_REACHED or 409 VIDEO_PROCESSING. This phase is called the point of no return: if it works, the project is alive.
nodes.norm_label: playback check order and error codes

nodes.label: Streaming Admin Panel (Vite + React + Tailwind)
nodes.rationale: Uploads through tus-js-client with a progress bar and a processing-status indicator polled every ten seconds.

nodes.label: Streaming Mobile App (Expo)
nodes.rationale: Includes a paywall on 402 and explicit handling of an expired link: catch the player error, re-request /playback and resume from the saved position. Live-device testing must cover Wi-Fi to mobile switching and poor networks, where quality should drop rather than stall.

nodes.label: Deferred Features (DRM, offline, recommendations, profiles, subtitles, live)
nodes.rationale: DRM waits until licensed content exists, and offline download is deferred because it requires DRM.
nodes.norm_label: deferred features (drm, offline, recommendations, profiles, subtitles, live)

nodes.label: Payment Provider Decision Point (Payme/Click/Uzum)
nodes.rationale: Integration is not written until the client names the provider and supplies test merchant access.

nodes.label: UzCasting Full UI/UX + Technical Specification V3
nodes.rationale: Gives every main function its own page, visual screen and explicit requirements. Stage 1 is Android with Uzbek/Russian, stage 2 iOS with English; core payments are Click, Payme, Uzum, Visa and Mastercard; design direction is dark luxury cinematic with neon purple/magenta and gold/cyan accents, and Figma is the final source of truth.
